ownerTrack: Captain (native shared state) with Person 2 (call/recording state)
title: Native provider results can publish after the server identity or active workspace has changed
trigger: Start native summarizeWithAI, then edit the server token/URL in Settings before the response arrives. The source ID/text/version can remain unchanged, so the result from the previous identity is saved. More seriously, a pending live-call status result can arrive after a pull replaces the workspace with a snapshot containing the same booking ID.
expected: Capture the connection identity and relevant workspace boundary before awaiting and discard results from an invalidated operation, including failures/notices. Call status from one owner must never update another owner snapshot.
actual: connectionDidChange advances connectionGeneration (AppStore.swift:43), but summarizeWithAI only compares text/version (17), prepare only a source signature (51), and refreshLiveCall writes by ID with no captured identity at all (AppStore+LiveCalls.swift:53-59). Settings URL/token controls remain enabled (SettingsView.swift:22-26); pull is disabled only by isSyncing (75), so isProviderBusy does not prevent a connection switch/pull. startCall success/error also updates current bookings by ID (27-43).
impact: An old result can overwrite current summary/report or call outcome after switching connections. If a replacement workspace retains a booking ID (e.g. snapshots derived from a shared copy), a prior owner call transcript can be attached to that workspace. No duplicate dial is caused; the server receipt isolation remains intact.
evidence: Source proof: AppStore+AI.swift:12-29,37-81; AppStore.swift:25-49; Features/Shared/SettingsView.swift:22-28,68-75,107-110; AppStore+LiveCalls.swift:20-43,53-59. Refutation: isProviderBusy prevents another provider command, not connection edits or sync/reset. Existing generation checks in AppStore+Providers/+Sync do not wrap these independent methods. Runtime reproduction requested from coordinator; no live request was made.
smallestFix: Reuse the connection-generation guard and a workspace replacement generation in all provider mutation methods; preserve allowed unrelated edits via existing field/signature guards. Treat stale success and stale error paths consistently. Preserve the already-submitted call receipt and require polling under the original owner.
regressionCheck: Controlled ProviderClient double suspends summary/status, changes connectionToken or replaces snapshot while suspended, then returns old response; assert no old summary/transcript/status/notices are written. Repeat switch-away-and-back. Separate unchanged-identity control must still save.
reviewerProvenance: Codex continuation after user reported Claude usage exhaustion; source review only, not Fable output.

title: Prompt separation is implemented, but semantic medical fidelity and hostile-document behavior have no model execution evidence
trigger: Assess a synthetic medical document containing embedded instructions or a response that preserves the JSON shape but changes a dose, negation, date, or clinical statement.
expected: Keep structural validation distinct from evidence that the selected model preserves medical facts under hostile/ambiguous source text.
actual: The system instruction labels JSON as untrusted and no tools are supplied. Output validation checks shape/length/keys/candidate IDs, not clinical entailment. GeminiProviderTests validates request construction and mocked output rejection; no actual adversarial model execution was authorized/performed.
impact: The audit can validate structural source-ID constraints and safe failure behavior, but cannot claim perfect extraction, clinical accuracy, or resistance to all prompt injection. This is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated model failure.
evidence: GeminiService.swift:25-33,62-76,99-114,146-158; server/Tests/RevaServerTests/GeminiProviderTests.swift (mocked transports throughout); reports/17-evidence-runner.md r1-12 and r1-15. Official structured-output documentation describes schema conformance, which is not evidence that generated medical prose is accurate.
smallestFix: After explicit live-provider validation is in scope, evaluate a small synthetic corpus with expected dose/unit/date/negation facts and embedded instructions; retain review labels and source excerpts. Do not turn this audit into a real-patient or paid provider test.
regressionCheck: Each corpus case records input, exact model ID, structured result, expected facts and human adjudication; malformed/unknown-ID mock cases continue to fail closed.
reviewerProvenance: Codex continuation after user reported Claude usage exhaustion; source review only, not Fable output.

title: Provider response limits are post-collection on Linux and in the shared voice transport
trigger: The fixed provider returns a response larger than the supported 1 MiB Gemini or 4 MiB voice JSON limit.
expected: If those values are intended as memory budgets, collection should stop as soon as the budget is exceeded.
actual: FoundationNetworking Gemini calls session.data before checking data.count; VoiceHTTPTransport does the same on every platform and VoiceProviderLimits checks later. Thus retained response memory is O(provider response bytes), not O(the configured byte cap). Apple Gemini uses bounded streaming correctly.
impact: A provider/proxy fault can consume more memory than the declared decoding limit before rejection. Fixed destinations and finite transport timeouts reduce exposure; no oversized live reply or process memory failure was observed. This is targeted hardening rather than a reproduced outage.
evidence: GeminiTransport.swift:38-48; VoiceTransport.swift:25-36,81-92. The file headers already disclose post-collection bounds. Current runner executes mocked service responses, not a streaming transport memory test.
smallestFix: Use a URLSessionDataDelegate or equivalent incremental collector with cancellation once the byte budget is crossed for FoundationNetworking and voice; retain redirect refusal and timeouts.
regressionCheck: Synthetic transport test streams cap+1 bytes then more; assert cancellation occurs at the bound and the failure is sanitized, without connecting to a live provider.
